outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: None that matter here; the failure is not about formatting, wording, or small precision issues.

Critical issues: (1) The agent did not provide any of the requested comparison outputs (no share prices, no market caps, no YTD values, no latest visible news headlines for either company). (2) The agent did not demonstrate opening Microsoft’s company page at all; screenshots show only a general market overview and unrelated search suggestions, with no MSFT/Microsoft page content. (3) For Apple, the only visible evidence is the search suggestions dropdown that includes “AAPL — Apple Inc · NASDAQ (US)” with a quoted price; there is no evidence the agent reached Apple’s dedicated company/quote page showing market cap, YTD, and Apple-specific news. (4) The agent claimed the DOM contained no Apple-specific stock info and that controls were non-hit-testable; screenshots contradict the strongest part of that claim because Apple ticker suggestions and prices are visible in the dropdown, and there is no clear visual evidence of a platform-level blocker (e.g., CAPTCHA, outage) preventing normal navigation.

Outcome assessment: The task’s primary deliverable is the Apple-vs-Microsoft comparison (including identifying which has the larger market cap). The agent terminated without retrieving the required data for either company and without producing the comparison or market-cap winner. From an average user’s perspective, this does not accomplish the task.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to use Google Finance to look up Apple and Microsoft, open each company’s page, extract four specific fields (current share price, market cap, YTD performance, and latest visible news headline), compare them side-by-side, and state which company has the larger market capitalization. A reasonable user would be flexible on minor formatting or whether the agent uses an equivalent finance source if Google Finance were genuinely blocked, but not flexible on missing the required fields, failing to open both company pages, or failing to identify the larger market cap based on actual retrieved data.
